correctness.rationale: For a single-one factor, a border exists exactly when both sides have nonzero zero runs. For a two-one factor, equal endpoint symbols give a one-letter border; when only the leading zero run is present, the only possible proper prefix ending in 1 is the run followed by the first 1, which is a suffix exactly when the run is at most the central gap. Reversal deals with a trailing run. This proves the occurrence counts, including the singletons of 11, with no deduplication by factor string. The disjoint gap classes sum to the stated series; [z^n]B counts (n-2)/3 < m <= (n-2)/2. Uniform gaps converge by simplex Riemann sums, and ties lie on area-zero lines. On Q=2 the inner gap is the simplex maximum, giving one third of its inclusion-exclusion CDF. On Q=1, requiring both outer gaps at least 1-t gives (2t-1)_+^2, with one third of the translated simplex with all gaps at least 1-t excluded. Integrals give conditional means 29/36 and 11/18 and the stated marginal mean. The independent raw substring prefix/suffix checker and separate expansion of the rational series agreed on all 3654 words of lengths 2–28; replay: /workspace/branches/4fc04731-0aed-42bc-94c7-65db87324ec8/independent_check.py. The source scripts and saved outputs were inspected but not executed; the bounded replay supplements the all-length proof.

value.rationale: In the first sparse binary family with interacting marker gaps, the number of optimal positions is genuine information beyond the already known optimal length and is the output size for all-occurrences reporting. The classification exposes the exceptional ties, gives their exact frequencies, and shows how optimum length differs between the two positive-probability multiplicity classes. This is a complete natural fixed-content refinement rather than a repeat of the marginal spectrum.
